note: P5-01 native continuation boundary prototype. Reverted; the prototype was isolated behind -Dzjs_native_continuation_proto and the default build was byte-unchanged.
hypothesis: inserting a non-tail native continuation boundary at the OP_call edge replaces explicit caller continuation save/restore and lowers ordinary sync call cost

design.entry: pushed exactly as the shipped path does
design.only_change: op_return yields .returned when machine.depth == vm.native_boundary_depth, so the value returns through a native return address instead of tail-calling the caller and republishing its state
design.isolation: build flag; Vm field is zero-sized when off; default build RC=0 and unchanged

boundary_hits_per_200_calls.note: only fib reaches the prototype arm; the others take leaf arms, making them predicted-zero controls

falsified.claim: P3-13 attributed 68% of the remaining gap to return, on the grounds that qjs restores through a C return address off an alloca frame while zjs maintains an explicit Machine frame stack
falsified.result: handing caller continuation to a native return address costs 6.95ns MORE per call, not 4.37ns less
falsified.correction: zjs's tail-call trampoline is already cheaper than a native boundary at this granularity. qjs's return is nearly free not because it uses the C stack but because its frame holds nothing that needs restoring - no arena mark, no catch target, no teardown shape, no continuation tag. That is a state-quantity problem, not a restore-mechanism problem.

phase_falsification_chain.claimed: argc step is the wrapper call boundary
Entry's four cache lines are special state
phase_falsification_chain.result: special state is 22 B and shares a line with hot fields

phase_falsification_chain.claimed: op_return's 208-byte frame is the extended chain

phase_falsification_chain.result: they also encode window-installed; three mutation paths

phase_falsification_chain.claimed: the call path is layout sensitive
the return gap is the missing native return address
phase_falsification_chain.result: a native boundary costs 6.95 ns more per call

conclusion: six falsifications converge: the remaining gap is neither shared control flow, nor layout, nor the restore mechanism, but the amount of state an ordinary frame carries - arena_mark 16, catch_target 16, this_value 16, five slices 80, Stack 40, none of which qjs has

recommended_next.reason: Frame/Stack representation redesign is the only remaining call-path direction, and it pairs a 107+ consumer change surface with no timing evidence that footprint is the bottleneck (P4-01c only excluded layout). fib_rec ~1.30x now has six falsifications behind it and is reasonably recorded as a structural constant of the current call model.

limits: single P0/P1 instance, no four-combination; the 24.8% regression is far outside build-instance spread (~0.5%)
entry/return/body not split - the total already regressed
throw and tail are not handled inside the boundary by design, though the throw probe shows the VM is not corrupted
Entry is still pushed per call; removing Entry and the tail chain together was not tested and would need Frame representation work first
